professors.name: Pat O'Neil
professors.title: Emeriti/Retired Faculty
professors.description: Professor Emeritus in the Department of Psychology (served 1974–2003). Expert in community psychology and ethical decision-making; authored 30+ publications and three books; taught History and Systems and ethics; supervised over 80 theses. Served as Chair of the Nova Scotia Board of Examiners in Psychology (1989–1991), President of the Canadian Psychological Association, editor of Canadian Psychology, Fellow of CPA, APA, and APS, and recipient of CAUT's Distinguished Academic Award. Deceased October 1, 2021.

professors.name: Lisa Price
professors.title: Emeriti/Retired Faculty
professors.description: Registered clinical psychologist and retired Acadia professor. Research focuses on sexual health, relationship violence, attachment and related psychophysiology; maintains private practice and collaborates widely.

professors.title: Philosophy
professors.description: My contribution to the SPT program, in addition to participation on theses and the colloquium series, has tended toward treatments of important historical figures in political theory. I have offered, most recently, a primary source course on the philosophy of Karl Marx. My general research background concerns figures from the Enlightenment, primarily Immanuel Kant.

professors.name: Andrew Biro
professors.title: Politics
professors.description: My research is mainly in the field of environmental political theory. In this field, we ask: what do the insights and methods of political theory have to tell us about contemporary environmental concerns? And how do contemporary environmental conditions affect the vocation of the political theorist? Two of my current research projects are on the politics of bottled water, and a book project (co-authored with Alice Cohen) on environmental politics in Canada. I am always interested in supervising MA projects in, and at the intersections of, critical theory, environmental politics, political e...

professors.name: Rachel Brickner
professors.title: Politics
research_areas: Workers' activism (women, migrants, public sector workers)
professors.description: In my research, I ask the broad question of how the relationship of worker-citizen is shaped and reshaped by political, economic, and social trends and the implications of this (re)shaping on democratic politics. More particularly, I use feminist theory and theories of citizenship and political economy to better understand the causes and outcomes of workers’ activism—particularly of women, public sector workers, and migrants, and with a geographic focus on the US, Canada, and Mexico. My current research project explores educators’ activism in the US and Canada through the lens of a feminist...

professors.name: James Brittain
professors.title: Sociology
professors.description: James J. Brittain, Ph.D. is a Professor within the Department of Sociology and faculty member of the Social & Political Thought graduate program at Acadia University. Through fields of social theory and political economy, his publications, research, and writing have been grounded in a critique of capitalist ideology and practice. Developing a discourse around the sociology of escape, his current work interrogates how inequitable class relations remain substantively unchallenged.

professors.name: Jesse Carlson
professors.title: Sociology
professors.description: Jesse Carlson is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Sociology and faculty member of the Social & Political Thought graduate program at Acadia University. Areas of research and supervision interest include cultural sociology, sociology of morality, critical theory, practice theory, theories of friendship and solidarity, the sociology of music.

professors.name: Fikir Haile
professors.title: Politics (starting July 2024)
professors.description: My research examines the inter-scalar governance of socio-environmental transformations in the Global South, with a focus on the African continent. Specifically, I am interested in understanding how the spatial expansion of capitalism transforms, reconfigures, and restructures urban environments across the globe broadly and in Africa specifically. More broadly, my research aims to identify the historical and ongoing processes that give rise to highly uneven global spaces, with a view to identifying avenues for decolonial and anti-imperialist futures. professors.name: Katie Mazer
professors.title: Cross-appointed, WGST & ESST
research_areas: Critical perspectives on work and unemployment
professors.description: My research examines the relationship between work, uneven development, and natural resource economies. I am generally pre-occupied with the power that work has over our lives and the ways work-related struggles are shaped by and remake the material world we call “nature.” My current book project examines the historical making of a mobile workforce in the Maritimes that travels long distances to work in resource extraction. professors.name: Can E. Mutlu
professors.title: Politics
professors.description: I am an Associate Professor of Global Politics at Acadia University, in Wolfville, Nova Scotia, Canada. I am the co-editor of Critical Methods in Security Studies: An Introduction (with Mark B. Salter) and Architectures of Security: Design, Control, Mobility (with Benjamin J. Muller). My recent research appears in Third World Quarterly, International Political Sociology, Global Governance, Millennium: Journal of International Studies, Comparative European Politics, European Journal of Social Theory, Eurasia Border Review, Environment and Planning D: Society and Space, and the Review of Inte...

professors.name: Kait Pinder
professors.title: English
professors.description: My primary areas of research are Canadian literature, the twentieth-century novel, and literary theory. In particular, my work examines how novelists use form, style, and genre to voice critical thought and philosophical debate. I am also interested in how aesthetic forms “think” about political and social relations. Currently, I am writing an introduction to feminisms and Canadian literature as well as a literary history of the impostor syndrome. I am happy to work with students who are also perplexed and preoccupied by the relationship between literature and politics, by questions of arti...

professors.name: Marc Ramsay
professors.title: Philosophy
research_areas: Parents' rights in the moral education of children
professors.description: My main research interests are in the philosophy of law and normative ethics. I work on issues such as children's rights, freedom of expression, judicial review, legal moralism, and damages in tort law. I am currently co-editing (with Jason Holt) a volume on philosophy and mixed martial arts (MMA). My teaching within SPT has focused on freedom of expression and judicial review.

professors.name: Nandini Thiyagarajan
professors.title: English & Theatre (on leave 2024-25)
professors.description: My research works at the intersection between postcolonial literature and theory, animal studies, and environmental humanities. I am interested in the relationship between race, animals, and the environment, and how this plays out in literature, culture, and politics.

professors.name: Inna Viriasova
professors.title: Politics
professors.description: My primary interests are in the fields of contemporary continental political philosophy (esp. political ontology), Non-Western and indigenous thought, critical theory, post-humanism and new materialism, biopolitics, and refugee studies. My research addresses the question of the limits of politics, seeking for positive ways of rethinking “the unpolitical” – the radical outside of politics – which forms the core of my recent monograph, At the Limits of the Political: Affect, Life, Things (RLI, 2018). professors.title: Politics
research_areas: Political Theory of War and Peace
professors.description: My research occurs at the intersection of Political Theory, International Politics, Art and Technology. In terms of political theory most of my research, broadly described, involves continental political thought (i.e., Deleuze, Foucault, Derrida, Virilio, Esposito. Agamben, Ranciere etc.) and contemporary off-shoots (eg., Butler, Brown, Grosz, Spivak, Mignolo, Charkabarty, Hacker, Massumi, Wolfe, Connolly, Shapiro etc.).
